models_evaluated: EHR-integrated OUD clinical decision support system with OUD/overdose risk score

links.outcome: Patient outcomes (MOUD days covered, overdose or death) versus usual care in cluster RCT
links.effect: Naloxone orders 1.4% vs 0.7% (OR 1.76); MOUD/referral orders 14.0% vs 9.4% (OR 1.48); no difference in MOUD days covered (rate ratio 1.00) or overdose/death rates.
links.quote: There were no differences in median (IQR) days covered by MOUD over 90 days postindex between intervention (84 [55-90] days) and usual care (83 [55-90] days; rate ratio, 1.00; 95% CI, 0.93-1.08) or in overdose or death rates during the intervention period.

unlisted_practices: EHR-integrated clinical decision support delivering personalized treatment recommendations to both patients and primary care clinicians to increase OUD diagnosis and treatment

screen.reason: Pragmatic cluster randomized clinical trial evaluating the clinical impact of an EHR-integrated CDSS incorporating risk scores to support OUD diagnosis and treatment in real primary care settings.
